args.text: ### Project Directory Setup Strewth, where do I start? With a directory, that’s where: somewhere to keep yer Rust code. Now, Rust doesn’t give a flyin’ toss where yer code lives, could be under the house with the redbacks for all it cares, but for the exercises and projects in this book, we reckon ya make a _projects_ directory in yer home directory and keep all yer projects in there, nice and tidy, so ya know where the lot is. So fire up a terminal and punch in these commands. They make a _projects_ directory, then a directory for the “Hello, world!” project inside it. Easy as. If yer on Linux, macOS, or PowerShell on Windows, it’s this lot: ```console $ mkdir ~/projects $ cd ~/projects $ mkdir hello_world $ cd hello_world ``` And if yer stuck with Windows CMD, ya poor bugger, it’s this: ```cmd > mkdir "%USERPROFILE%\projects" > cd /d "%USERPROFILE%\projects" > mkdir hello_world > cd hello_world ``` ### Rust Program Basics Next up, ya make a new source file and call it _main.rs_. Rust files always end in the _.rs_ extension, every bloody one of ’em. Got more than one word in yer filename? Then the usual go is to whack an underscore between ’em so they don’t run together. So it’s _hello_world.rs_, not _helloworld.rs_, which looks like a sneeze. Now crack open that _main.rs_ file ya just made and punch in the code from Listing 1-1. Here it is, all three lines of it: ```rust fn main() { println!("Hello, world!"); } ``` Save it, then nip back to yer terminal window in the _~/projects/hello_world_ directory. On Linux or macOS, punch in these commands to compile and run the file: ```console $ rustc main.rs $ ./main Hello, world! ``` On Windows, mind, it’s `.\main` instead of `./main`, cos Windows has always gotta be different: ```powershell > rustc main.rs > .\main Hello, world! ``` Doesn’t matter what operating system yer on, the string `Hello, world!` should pop up in the terminal. And if ya don’t get that output? No dramas. Have a squiz back at the [“Troubleshooting”][troubleshooting] part of the Installation section for where to get a hand. But if `Hello, world!` did come up? Well, good on ya, mate! You’ve officially written a Rust program. Fair dinkum. That makes ya a Rust programmer—welcome to the club! First round’s on you.
